title: What If a Skyscraper Melted Cars? In 2013 One in London Did

scenes.text: What if a skyscraper could melt a car? In 2013, one in London did. By accident.
The tower at 20 Fenchurch Street, nicknamed the Walkie Talkie, has a south face of glass that curves inward.
A curved mirror focuses light. That summer, the glass gathered the sun into a beam and aimed it at the street below.
A parked Jaguar's panels and wing mirror melted. Shop carpets scorched, paint blistered, and tiles cracked.
The developers paid the driver 946 pounds, put up a screen, and said the sun would line up for only two to three weeks.
The twist: the same architect's hotel in Las Vegas had done it three years earlier, singeing guests' hair by the pool.

description:
What if a glass skyscraper focused the sun like a magnifying glass?
In the summer of 2013 the tower at 20 Fenchurch Street in London, nicknamed the Walkie Talkie, did exactly that. Its south-facing glass wall is concave, so on sunny days it acted as a curved mirror and concentrated sunlight onto a nearby street. Parts of a parked Jaguar XJ, including panels and a wing mirror, melted; shop owners reported scorched carpets, blistered paint and shattered tiles. The developers paid the car's owner 946 pounds, put up a temporary screen at street level and said the effect was caused by the sun's elevation at that time of year and would last two to three weeks. The architect, Rafael Vinoly, had also designed the Vdara hotel in Las Vegas, where in 2010 a similar curved glass face focused sunlight on the pool deck, melting plastic cups and singeing guests' hair.
What should we run through next?
